newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says RBNZ's MPS consistent with Budget.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says RBNZ's MPS consistent with Budget.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Friday the contents of the Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Statement, released earlier in the day, were broadly consistent with the government's budget delivered on Thursday.

Bolger also told a post-budget luncheon at the Auckland Chamber of Commerce that the RBNZ's forecasts of core inflation remaining well within the 0-3 percent target band over the forecast period would be positive for interest rates and the currency.

"The budget we delivered yesterday builds on the momentum of all that New Zealand has achieved over the last half dozen years, and it guarantees the momentum of a growing, successful economy," Bolger said.
Since then, he said, the Reserve Bank had issued its June Monetary Policy Statement, "the contents of which were broadly consistent with the budget".

"As you'd expect, the bank's forecasts differ slightly from the Treasury's in some respects," Bolger said. Where Treasury was projecting growth of 4.2 percent in 1998/99, the RBNZ was forecasting 3.6 percent.
"Whether you choose to put more store in the bank's projections, those of Treasury or those of private forecasters, its doesn't change the essential story.
"And it is a good story," Bolger said.
He said the RBNZ's inflation forecasts would be positive for the New Zealand dollar and interest rates.
"The bank expects underlying inflation to stay well within the 0-3 percent band over the forecast period. This will be positive for interest rates and the currency.
"And good for business and home owners," Bolger added.
